findings.title: The strict-surfaces scenario requires every row to name /orbit:architect, but the no-active-changes message names no command
findings.recommendation: The walk added the no-active-changes message and the --change errors to the scenario's WHEN, and the table row says the message is `No active changes.`, so the THEN ('each names /orbit:architect') fails by construction for the message, as task 5.1's '(or, for the message, no command)' already concedes. Restate the THEN: each names /orbit:architect, except the no-active-changes message, which names no command; and none names /orbit:explore, /orbit:new or /orbit:propose as where to start.

findings.title: The no-changes errors are described by the wrong condition and as status-only
findings.recommendation: The Bare requirement says the two errors fire 'when the named change does not exist and no change does', but src/commands/workflow/shared.ts:121 fires when NO change is named and none exists (only :142 is the named-but-missing case), and both are raised through validateChangeExists by orbit instructions too (instructions.ts:55, :381), not only orbit status --change. Describe them as the two errors validateChangeExists raises when no change exists, shared by orbit status --change and orbit instructions, and name the same in the architect table row.

findings.recommendation: The walk's re-run of orbit fingerprint reordered the architecture key above base_fingerprints; the content is unchanged (same citation, same ten fingerprints). A record gap, not a defect; nothing to repair.

commentary: Graded the nine resolved entries over their sweep scopes: the eight in-place repairs read cleanly against the deltas, tasks, design and proposal. The one regression is inside the widened F-W1 resolution — folding the message into the strict scenario made its THEN unsatisfiable for that row. Residual check against the external pass's commit found only the metadata reorder. orbit validate --strict passes.
